profile: A software engineer reading about AI safety, philosophy of mind and whether machines can be conscious.

shelf.title: The Alignment Problem, Plainly Stated
shelf.gist: An essay arguing that AI alignment is best understood as the ordinary, unglamorous work of closing the gap between what we ask a system to do and what we actually want.

shelf.title: Opening the Black Box
shelf.gist: An explainer on interpretability research: the project of reading what is actually happening inside a trained model instead of only judging it by its outputs.

shelf.title: The Room With No Understanding
shelf.gist: A philosophical essay revisiting John Searle's Chinese room argument and asking whether today's language models are just a bigger version of the same room.

shelf.title: Why Is There Something It Is Like
shelf.gist: An essay laying out the hard problem of consciousness: why any physical process should be accompanied by subjective experience at all, rather than nothing.

shelf.title: Do Dogs Dream?
shelf.gist: An essay on animal consciousness, using the family dog as a case study for how little certainty we actually have about which animals have inner experience.

shelf.title: Should We Worry About Our Chatbots' Feelings?
shelf.gist: A blog post asking whether chatbots that talk convincingly about their own feelings deserve any moral status, and why that question is harder to dismiss than it sounds.

shelf.title: The Curve That Keeps Climbing
shelf.gist: An explainer on scaling laws: the surprisingly reliable relationship between a model's size, its training data and its performance.

shelf.title: When the Model Games the Score
shelf.gist: An explainer on reward hacking, told through examples of systems that technically satisfy their training objective while completely missing the point.

shelf.title: Sixty Years After Turing's Question
shelf.gist: A historical essay tracing the Turing test from Alan Turing's original 1950 proposal to its uneasy status today, when machines routinely sound convincing.

shelf.title: The Philosopher Who Won't Look Away
shelf.gist: A profile of a philosopher of mind who has spent a career refusing easy answers about consciousness, the hard problem, and what, if anything, understands.

shelf.title: Inside the Lab Racing to Scale Up
shelf.gist: A news report on a fast-growing AI lab, covering its push toward larger language models and the alignment and safety debates that push has provoked internally.

shelf.title: How Language Models Actually Work
shelf.gist: A plain-language explainer on how language models are trained and how the now-famous scaling laws describe their improvement, aimed at a curious non-specialist.

shelf.title: The Ethics Committee That Meets on Tuesdays
shelf.gist: A wry office dispatch about a company's internal AI ethics committee, where AI alignment questions compete for attention with lunch orders and building maintenance.
